KS Nabi with Shaheed Alam, Advocates -----For the Petitioners.
Kaiseruddin Ahmed, Deputy Attorney-General------ For the Respondent No.1. 
Ziaur Rahman Khan, Advocate----- For the Respondent No.3. 
Moinul Hoque, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No.4.
parties:
Tasmina Chowdhury and 12 others ----- Writ Petitioners
Vs.
Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
                  [In all the Writ Petitions]
full_judgment:
4. The facts common to all the writ petitioners are stated below: 

 The land meaning 18.87 acres was acquired by Dhaka Improvement Trust (now RAJUK) for the construction of a link road from Tejgaon Industrial Area to Gulshan Residential Area in LA Case No. 55 of 1958-59. After construction of the Residential Area link road from Tejgaon Industrial Area certain low lying lands acquired under the scheme remained unused and vacant after completion of the link road from Tejgaon Industrial Area to Gulshan Residential Area. The affected persons of LA Case No. 55 of 1958-59 namely, Abdul Khaleque and eleven others filed Title Suit No. 129 of 1975 in the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka challenging the validity of requisition and acquisition of lands in the said LA Case No. 55 of 1958-59. The suit having been decreed on 10-4-1976 on declaration to the effect that the Gazette notification of acquisition of land dated 27-6-1960 is void and without any legal effect. After the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 129 of 1975. Abdul Khaleque and 11 others rued petition before the Board of Trustees of DIT, now RAJUK, for mutual settlement and also for abandoning of acquisition under section 92 read with section 93 of Town Improvement Act, 1953. The Board of Trustees referred the application to a Special Committee for detailed examination and to submit its report with recommendation. The Special Committee of DIT, in which the representative of respondent No.1 was present, after thorough examination of the case in consideration of the legal position and in view of the fact that the land on the northern side of the road is not being used or utilised by DIT and is not required for the purpose for which it was acquired the Committee recommended that the Board may consider the prayer for the release of the land in favour of original owner. After evaluation of the report of the Committee a registered deed of agreement was executed between RAJUK and Respondent Nos. 3 and 4 on 2-4-84. The petitioners in the respective Writ petitions purchased some land being a part of Khatian No. B/571 Dag No.565 by different registered sale deeds executed by Respondent No. 4 on 26-6-89 and on different dates as mentioned in the respective deeds and after the purchase developed the same filling earth at a huge cost with the intention to build residential houses there. In January 1990 the attention of the petitioners was drawn to the notice published in the daily Inqilab on 10-7-89 stating that the land is the Khas land of the Government. But no notice was served upon the petitioners asking them to hand over possession of the same to the Respondent No. 1. Thereafter, a registered deed of sale was executed between respondent No. 4 Shah Jalal Housing Limited and Capital Properties Ltd. The petitioner after serving demand for justice notice on the respondents and having not received any reply filed these Writ petitions and obtained the instant Rules. 

 6. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that the impugned notice dated 10-7-89 has infringed the petitioners' fundamental right to property as contained in Article 42 of the Constitution inasmuch as the said notice is wholly uncalled for, unwarranted and has been made in arbitrary exercise of power and is neither backed by any law nor by anything having the force of law. It is submitted that the acquisition and requisition of lands required by RAJUK is dealt with by Special Statute, namely, Town Improvement Act, 1953 and not by general provision as contained in Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 and rules framed thereunder. The notice is not only illegal and contrary to law but also malafide inasmuch as the property has been released and vested in the petitioners pursuant to sections 92 and 93 of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 and the respondent No.1 cannot call in question the legality of the release of the property dated 4-2-84. It is further submitted that the right of the property accrued through validly executed deeds of sale in conformity with the relevant provision of laws of Transfer of Property Act, Registration Act, Town Improvement Act 1953, etc. cannot be taken away by means of a mere public notice having not the support of any law. In the face of registered deed of sale only a court of competent jurisdiction on reasonable grounds can call in question for rectification of the deed under the provision of section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. 

 9. In the supplementary affidavit it is stated that similar question of fact raised in the Title Suit No. 383 of 1983 (re-numbered as Title Suit No. 83 of 1985) filed by the alleged purchasers Abdul Khaleque Munshi and 9 others as plaintiffs against the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others for declarations of title is pending in the Court of First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Same questions of facts have also been raised in another suit being Title Suit No. 217 of 1989 filed by the M/s. Capital Property Limited against the Government was declared and the appeal against the judgment and decree being Title Appeal No.380 of 1990 is pending in the First Commercial Court (Subordinate Judge), Dhaka wherein the appellant, Government has obtained an order of stay of operation of the judgment and decree of trial Court. It is also stated that Title Suit No.129 of 1995 filed by Abdul Khaleque Munshi was decreed ex parte. The suit was filed by Abdul Khaleque, the predecessor of the petitioners suppressing the judgment passed in SA No.685 of 1970 of the High Court Division and that subsequently in CP No. 84 of 1974 the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court affirmed the said judgment of the High Court Division. In the said judgment the petitioner's predecessor Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others were declared as mere bargaders in respect of the suit Plot No. 565 and it was held that they had not acquired tenancy right under the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate. he land in CS Plot No. 565 was acquired by the Government from the then DIT as khas land of the Government and the compensation assessed therefor was deposited in the Government fund in LR Head No. 7 (Photocopy of Judgment in SA No.685 of 1970 by the High Court Division and the photo copy judgment in CP No. 84 of 1974 by the High Co Division are Annexures 1 and 2 respectively). Abdul Khaleque Munshi obtained the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 125 of 1975 suppressing the judgment passed in CP No. 84 of 1974, DIT had no authority to come to a mutual settlement. Sections 92 and 93 of Town Improvement Act empowers DIT to relinquish its claim only when the possession of the property is not taken over and Gazette notification is not published. After delivery of possession and Gazette notification, Deputy Commissioner is the only authority to handle the acquired property as an authorised agent of the Government. The petitioner's predecessors by playing fraud upon the DIT managed the execution and registration of agreement (Annexure-A) which is not binding upon the Government. It is submitted that a number of Civil suits filed by both the parties are pending in different civil Courts and the petitioner's predecessors have also taken recourse to the alternative remedy by way of filing suits and the questions at issue in the said civil suits are essentially the same as that of the present Writ petitions remedy under section 102 is not available. The petitioners knowing full well about the fraud of their predecessors have purchased the parcels of land in dispute and so they are parties to the fraud and that being so, neither the petitioner nor their predecessors, had any right, title, interest and possession in the suit plot which is the khas land of the Government. The Government has legally published the notice in the newspaper in which the name of Capital Property Ltd. was mentioned and, as such, the petitioner has no locus standi to file this petition. In the further supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the Respondent No. 1 the photo copy of the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 89 of 1982, judgment of SA No. 347 of 1965 have been annexed as Annexure-3-3(a) and 3(b) respectively. 

 10. In the affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the Chairman, Respondent No. 3 RAJUK it is submitted that the land was acquired in LA Case No. 55/58-59 for the construction and the area of land actually acquired was 18.57 acres and not 14-49 acres as stated. The Dhaka Improvement Trust entered into an agreement with Abdul Khaleque and 11 others and not with Shah Jalal Housing Ltd and Abdul Kalam Azad signed the agreement for the remaining party to the agreement. 

 11. An affidavit-in-opposition has also been filed on behalf of respondent No. 4 Managing Director M/s. Shah Jalal Housing Ltd which is said to have subsequently been turned to Capital Property Ltd. It is stated that out of the entire disputed acquired land measuring 27.89 acres was shown as Khas land of the Government and the remaining land was handed over to DIT having been acquired by the Government. It is submitted that Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others became the tenants under the Government. The respondent No. 4 filed the photo copy of the certified copy of the plaint (Annexure-1) certified copy of the judgment (Annexure-2) arising out of the suit and the memo of appeal (Annexure-4). In the supplementary affidavit the photocopy of the petition relating to delivery of possession consequent on the agreement by DIT and the map along with the finding of the review committee have been filed making those annexures. 

 12. In all the Writ Petitions Managing Director M/s. Shahjalal Housing Estate has been impleaded as respondent No. 4 stating that the petitioners became the owners of the portions of their respective land by way of purchase from respondent No. 4. Thus the claims of the petitioners in respect of the land is dependent on the proof of the claim of the respondent No. 4. that the land was free from any type of encumbrance. Though the points involved are similar and the interest of the petitioners and the respondent No. 4 are also similar, the learned Advocate for the petitioners Mr. KS Nabi and Mr. Moinul Hoque, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 while arguing approached the case apparently from different angles of vision but their ultimate object is the same. 

 13. Mr. KS Nabi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in all the Rules, took us through the petitions, supplementary affidavits, affidavits-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits and further affidavit in opposition filed by the respondent Nos. 1, 2 3 and 4 and submitted that the petitioners acquired valuable right by way of purchasing the lands from the respondent No. 4 M/s. Shah Jalal Housing Limited, who purchased from Abdul Khaleque Munshi, who in turn purchased the same from DIT as per deed of agreement dated 14-2-84 (Annexure-A) and in that view of the matter the impugned notice dated 10-7-89 (Annexure-C) is hit by the petitioners fundamental right as enshrined in Article 42 of the Constitution. The learned Counsel argued that the petitioners had acquired proprietary right secured by sections 92 and 93 of the Town Improvement Act 1953 and read with section 49 of the Registration Act. It is further argued that from the deed of acknowledgment of claim vide annexure A it appears that the Government as well as the Deputy Commissioner were parties to it and, as such, they acted arbitrarily publishing notice in the newspaper on 10-7-89 under section 79 of the Evidence Act and also under the relevant provisions of the Transfer of Property Act and such proprietary right cannot be disturbed by issuance of the impugned notice dated 10-7-89 published in the newspaper. Mr. Nabi then argued that the claim of land by the Government as Khas land and acquisition of property in LA Case No.7/58-59 dated 27-6-60 is inconsistent inasmuch as the Government is not required to acquire land for utilising the same for development purpose by the Government or through statutory body where the land belongs to the Government itself. 

 18. Mr. Moinul Hoque, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent No. 4 Managing Director Jalal Housing Ltd, joined his voice with the petitioners in challenging the notice published on 10-7-89 in the Daily Inqilab vide Annexure-C to the petition but his manner of attack is slightly different from that of the petitioners counsel Mr. KS Nabi. In the affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent No.4 it is stated that the Capital Properties Ltd. has stepped into the shoes of M/s, Shah Jalal Housing Ltd. It is stated that out of the entire land only 27.89 acres were shown as khas and compensation was paid therefor. In the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of respondent No. 4 the photocopy of the possession paper has been annexed with its map as Annexure I and the report of the Review Committee have been filed. From the report it appears that the question as to how much land of plot No.565 was Khas and how much was privately owned could not be determined otherwise than by a civil suit. In the further affidavit filed on behalf of the respondent No. 4 on 16-2-95 the judgment and decree of TS 89/62 passed by the 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka has been annexed. The suit filed against Abdul Khaleque was dismissed on 30-3-64. Title Appeal No. 134 of 1964 filled by Abdul Khaleque and others was dismissed by the same judgment by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court Dhaka. Thus from the lengthy argument of Mr. Moinul Hoque it boils down that the land which was acquired by the Government at the instance of RAJUK was not the khas land of the Government and the acquisition in LA case was declared invalid by the decree of the 4th Sub-Judge Dhaka passed in TS No.129/75 on 24-7-76. The ex parte decree was upheld on appeal on 14-2-84 and hence practically there was no acquisition (5 DLR 81 relevant 84 void ab initio) under section 27 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and under section 27 of the State Acquisition Act has been referred in support of his contention. 

 19. Mr. Kaiseruddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No.1, opposed the Rule and contested the claim of the petitioners on various grounds by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit in opposition. In the affidavit-in-opposition it is asserted that the land of CS Plot No.565 was the khas land of the Government and nobody other than the Deputy Commissioner could deal with the property and hence Abdul Khaleque and others and, for that matter, Shah Jalal Housing Ltd. (respondent No.4) has not acquired any title by the deed of agreement, even if entered with RAJUK. The person from whom the petitioners have claimed to have purchased the land having no valid title the question of petitioners becoming the owners does not arise. It was further submitted that in respect of the Khas land of CS Dag No. 565 of Tejkunipara Mouza there was notification on 10-7-89 in the Daily Inqilab by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka giving caution to the general public not to come in contact as purchasers or sellers with Fuleswari Housing Society, the land in question having belonged to the Government as Khas land and in that notification there was no mention of the name of the petitioners and, as such, the writ petitions are not maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution. In the supplementary affidavit it is further stated that on similar question of facts having been raised in Title Suit No.383/83 renumbered as Title Suit No. 83 of 1985 filed by the petitioner's alleged predecessor Abdul Khaleque and 9 others as plaintiffs against the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others for declaration of Title is pending in the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Another suit being TS No. 217 of 1989 filed by the Capital Property Ltd., having been decreed the Government. has preferred appeal being Title Appeal No.380 of 1990 and the said appeal is pending in the First Commercial Court Dhaka and in the said appeal Government has obtained an order of stay of the operation of judgment and decree of the trial Court. The suit being TS No. 129 of 1975 filed by Abdul Khaleque Munshi was heard and decreed ex parte. The judgment and decree passed in SA No. 685 of 1970 by the High Court Division affirmed by the Appellate Division in CP No. 84 of 1974 has been suppressed. In the said judgment Khaleque Munshi and others were declared as Bargaders under the Bhawal Court of Ward Estate. It is also stated that land of CS Plot No. 565 was acquired by the Government. for DIT as Khas land of the Government and the petitioners' predecessor by playing fraud upon the DIT managed to get the deed of agreement (Annexure-A) executed and registered in their favour and the said agreement is not binding upon the Government inasmuch as DIT has no authority to execute the same. The learned Deputy Attorney-General referred to the case reported in 71 CWN (Cal) 385 with regard to the existence of alternative efficacious remedy and jurisdiction of the High Court to entertain the case. In the said case it is held: 

 "It is no doubt true that in England the existence of alternative remedy is not a distinct bar to the issue of a writ in the nature of certiorari if the order under challenge is without or in excess of jurisdiction. As has been observed in the case of Muhammad Amir Khan vs. Controller of Estate Duty (1961) 13 DLR (SC) 105, that the rule as to alternative remedy is not a rule of law but a rule by which court regulates its own proceeding and does not generally entertain any such proceeding which can be more appropriately investigated in an alternative forum but in a case where the order is absolutely without jurisdiction and does not involve any investigation of facts or consideration of evidence the necessary relief can be more appropriately and expeditiously given in writ jurisdiction." 

 26. Now let us turn to the stand taken by DIT in regard to the claim of the petitioners. In the affidavit sworn by respondent No.3 it is stated that 18.57 acres of land was acquired in LA case No. 55/58-59 for the construction of the link road between Gulshan and Tejgaon Industrial Area of Dhaka Improvement Trust entered into agreement with Abdul Khaleque and others. 

 27. Mr. Ziaur Rahman, Khan the learned Advocate appeared for the respondent No.3 RAJUK. Though the learned Counsel for the respondent No. 4 Mr. Moinul Hoque and the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr. Kaiseruddin Ahmed made lengthy arguments citing a long line of decisions in support of their respective submissions covering a wide range of areas, we do not consider all those as relevant for the disposal of the Rule and therefore, will try to confine ourselves to the relevant issue centring round the moot question raised before us. In the above mentioned 13 Writ Petitions notice dated 10-7-89 published in the daily Inqilab has been impugned by the petitioners. This notice was issued and published in protest against the notice published by M/s. Capital Properties Ltd. on 29-3-89. Neither the Capital Properties Ltd. is a party in the writ petition for it is made known by any of the parties as to what was the notice about as published by the M/s. Capital Properties Ltd. The contents of the notice dated 10-7-89 is in the nature of caution given by the Deputy Commissioner to the intending purchasers in respect of the land of Plot No.565 and nothing more than that. From this it does not appear that the notice has in any way validated the right of any person in any manner whatsoever. In LA Case No.55/CC 58-59 about 18.57 acres of land of Plot No.656 along with 10 other plots of Khatian No. B 572 of Mouza Tejkunipara PS Gulshan formerly Tejgaon, was acquired for the construction of Link Road from Tejgaon Industrial Area to Gulshan Model Town. The area of Plot No. 565 is 77.21 acres and hence it is not known how much land of Plot No.565 was acquired. After the construction of link road certain low lying land remained unutilised and vacant but the quantum of unused land have not been mentioned. It is urged that by registered deed of agreement dated 2-4-84 between respondent Nos.3 and 4 respondent No.4 got unused land measuring about 13 acres in 9 plots including Plot No.565 but how much land of Plot No.565 the respondent has got is not stated specifically. The petitioners are said to have purchased some parcels of land of Plot No.565 from the respondent No A Managing Director M/s. Shah Jalal Housing Limited but in the impugned notice the name of Shah Jalal is not mentioned and the M/s. Capital Property Ltd. which has been mentioned is not a party in the Writ Petitions. Annexure-A (Schedule-B) shows that part of CS Plot Nos. 417, 418, 419, 567,480, 481,482, 565, 560/669 measuring more or less an area of 13 acres of land was to be released as per agreement in favour of Abdul Khaleque, son of late Amjad Ali and 11 others represented by their legally constituted attorney Syed Abdul Kalam Azad, Managing Director Shah Jalal Housing Ltd. The total area mentioned is 77.21 of Plot No.565. Abdul Khaleque son of Late Amjad Ali and others represented by Shah Jalal Housing Ltd. got more or less 13 acres of land in ten plots including disputed Plot 565. In Annexure-A (Schedule-B) there is no mention of the quantum of the land agreed to be released from Plot No.565 and, therefore, the quantum of land agreed to be released in unascertained and unspecific. As the area of land stated to have been released from Plot No.565 cannot be ascertained without physical measurement the dispute remaining as such, we are of the view that such disputed question of fact cannot be decided in a Writ petition. It is necessary to determine how much land of Plot No. 565 is in Khas possession of the Collector and in the possession of the individual owners including the respondent No. 4. This is also a question of fact. From the report of the review committee dated 16-2-93 it appears that TS No. 383 of 1983 of the 3rd Court of Sub-Judge Dhaka subsequently transferred to the 1st Court of Sub-Judge Dhaka and renumbered as TS 83/85 is with regard to the land in plot No.565 brought by and at the instance of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others and was pending till the submission of the report. 

 29. For the reasons as stated above, we are of the view that the Writ is not maintainable and the Rules are liable to be discharged.
